newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Advance troops land in Albania, king expected.
newsitem.headline: Advance troops land in Albania, king expected.

text.p: Albanians awaited the arrival of their long-exiled king on Saturday as advance troops from a multinational security force deployed in the lawless Balkan state.
King Leka I was due to arrive at Tirana airport at 1 p.m. (1100 GMT) on a private plane from South Africa.
"He will call on Albanians to put an end to violence and to put their guns away," Guri Durollari of the Legality Movement Party told Reuters late on Friday.

Italy said the bulk of its troop contingent would move into Albania from Tuesday at the head of a 6,000-strong multinational force to protect distribution of emergency food and medicines after six weeks of violent unrest.

Some 100 Italian troops had arrived since Friday and most of them were protecting Tirana airport and adapting it for round-the-clock operations, an official source said. A unit of some 20 men arrived in the western port of Durres on Friday.
Some 10 Spanish infantrymen, based in Malaga, and a few Greek, Turkish and Austrian soldiers had reached Tirana to plot the arrival of the multinational force, military sources and residents said.
An advance unit of about 100 French soldiers arrived in the southern Italian port of Brindisi on Friday, officials said.

Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta was expected to hold talks with officials in Tirana later on Saturday to discuss the deployment of the force and other bilateral issues, official sources said.
Rome has committed about 2,500 troops to the U.N.-approved force, the first of its kind to be led by Italy.
Albania sank into near-anarchy after popular get-rich-quick investment schemes collapsed six weeks ago.

Local media reported on Saturday that most of the 279 people killed and more than 598 wounded since March 1 were in the south. The figures do not include an estimated 80 killed when a refugee boat sank on March 28.
The southern port city of Vlore was the centre of violence, with 60 killed and 400 wounded.

King Leka, 58, who was only a few days old when his father, King Zog, fled the country with his family in 1939, would call for a referendum to let Albanians decide whether or not to restore the monarchy, Durollari said.
"He is here to settle. He is here to stay," he added.

Leka, tall and bespectacled, only once tried to visit Albania, in 1993. He was unceremoniously bundled back onto a plane within 24 hours on the grounds that his passport marked "Kingdom of Albania" was invalid.
Durollari said President Sali Berisha had reiterated his approval of Leka's visit during a meeting in Tirana on Friday.
The violence in Albania has continued unabated.
The state-run news agency ATA said assailants using automatic weapons shot dead a 43-year-old man in Tirana on Friday. The motive was unclear.
Occasional bursts of gunfire rang out in Tirana on Saturday, but were more frequent on Friday night during a curfew from 8 p.m. until 7 a.m.
A 16-year-old boy was killed in a village near Vlore on Friday when a grenade he was playing with exploded, police said. A 15-year-old boy was seriously injured.
